claims.claim: CDF on Databricks: delta.enableChangeDataFeed, readChangeFeed, startingVersion, table_changes.

concept_html:
When silver changes, gold should reprocess only the rows that changed, not the whole table. Change data feed (CDF) makes a Delta table record row-level changes for every write.

Turn it on per table:

ALTER TABLE research_prod.research_silver.nat_respondents
SET TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true);

Read the changes since a version:

changes = (
    spark.read.option("readChangeFeed", "true")
    .option("startingVersion", last_version + 1)
    .table("research_prod.research_silver.nat_respondents")
)

Each row carries three extra columns:

  • _change_type: insert, update_preimage (the row before an update), update_postimage (the row after), or delete.
  • _commit_version and _commit_timestamp: which commit made the change.

Two rules make CDF consumers correct:

  1. Drop update_preimage rows before you use the changes. An update produces two rows, old and new. Keep the old one and every updated respondent is counted twice.
  2. Keep one row per key: the latest by _commit_version. A respondent updated in three commits since your last run appears three times.

Track progress. Either store the last processed version in a state table, or read the feed as a stream (readStream with readChangeFeed) and let the checkpoint remember it. Change data only exists from the version where you enabled it. Asking for an earlier version fails with DELTA_MISSING_CHANGE_DATA. VACUUM also removes old change files after the retention window.

For gold, collect the waves and subgroups the changes touch, then recompute just those aggregates. Aggregates cannot be patched row by row.

lines: CURRENT_STATE = ["insert", "update_postimage"]
def read_changes(spark: SparkSession, table: str, last_processed_version: int) -> DataFrame:
"""Row changes committed after last_processed_version."""
return (
spark.read.option("readChangeFeed", "true")
.option("startingVersion", last_processed_version + 1)
.table(table)
)
def latest_state(changes: DataFrame, keys: list[str]) -> DataFrame:
"""One row per key: its newest change, excluding pre-images."""
window = Window.partitionBy(*keys).orderBy(F.col("_commit_version").desc())
return (
changes.filter(F.col("_change_type") != "update_preimage")
.withColumn("_rank", F.row_number().over(window))
.filter(F.col("_rank") == 1)
.drop("_rank")
)
def touched_waves(changes: DataFrame) -> list[str]:
"""Waves with any change: the only gold waves to recompute."""
return sorted(r.wave_id for r in changes.select("wave_id").distinct().collect())

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def latest_state(changes: DataFrame, keys: list[str]) -> DataFrame:
    """One row per key: its newest change, excluding update pre-images.

    Args:
        changes: Rows read with readChangeFeed.
        keys: Columns identifying one row of the source table.

    Returns:
        The newest insert, update_postimage or delete per key.
    """
    window = Window.partitionBy(*keys).orderBy(F.col("_commit_version").desc())
    return (
        changes.filter(F.col("_change_type") != "update_preimage")
        .withColumn("_rank", F.row_number().over(window))
        .filter(F.col("_rank") == 1)
        .drop("_rank")
    )

title: Change data feed, so downstream layers read only what changed
why_html:
A gold job rebuilds weighted metrics for every wave every night: 180 waves, 40 minutes. Most nights, only one wave changed. When a late correction arrives mid-afternoon, the team cannot refresh gold before the client call, because a full rebuild takes too long.

With CDF on silver, the job reads the day's changes, finds the one wave they touch, and recomputes it in under two minutes. The same job also stops double counting, because it drops update_preimage rows before aggregating.
